title: methods.v1: the method table of the control API
description: The method table of the control API, version 1: one row for every method, kept as data (methods.table.v1.json beside this file validates against this schema's root), and for every method the schema of its params and of everything it can answer. A request is {method, params}; a recorded request with its answer is an exchange ($defs/exchange). RULES, frozen with the table. (1) Unknown and unbuilt. A name that is not in the table is answered 'method_unknown'. A name that is in the table and has no handler in the running daemon is answered 'unsupported' with detail 'not_implemented'; methods.list says which are implemented now. (2) Idempotency. Every mutating method except run.start and run.stop takes a command_id. There is one identity domain: (tenant, method, command_id), kept durably across restarts, with no part that changes at a restart. run.start keeps client_key, which is its command id, under that name on every surface. run.stop takes neither a key nor a revision: an emergency Stop never needs fresh state. A client that is a model does not mint unique ids, so on a surface a model drives the server mints the id and hands it to the caller. (3) Order of checks. The caller is authorized first. Then the receipt is looked up: the same id with the same payload digest returns the first answer, even if the revision it named is stale by now; the same id with another digest is 'conflict' (detail command_id_reused). Only then is expected_revision or expected_turn_id checked: stale is 'conflict' (detail stale_revision or stale_turn). A live turn is 'busy'. A missing driver flag is 'unsupported', before any side effect. The payload digest is over the method and its params without the command_id. (4) Who may Stop. PROVISIONAL, the owner's decision. run.stop needs a currently held 'run' scope. An owner or a device holding 'run' may stop any run, including one whose record names no principal (every run from before version 1): no run is stranded. A session principal may stop only runs of its own session and of the sessions it started. A caller without 'run' cannot stop. The daemon's own recovery Stop is not a client's call and no authorizer applies to it. (5) Approvals. approval.list returns summaries and shows nothing. approval.open records that a surface displayed the prompt. approval.answer without an open record for the current revision is refused 'prompt_not_shown'. Neither is ever offered as an MCP tool. (6) Params are closed for a caller: a conforming client sends only what is listed. Today's daemon ignores a key it does not know on run.start; it never stores one. A principal, an owner, a budget's reservation and a session's identity are never taken from params.

method_name.description: Every method of version 1. A name that is not here is answered method_unknown.

code.description: Every code an answer can carry. The first five are not refusals.

scope.description: What a caller must hold. 'read': look. 'run': start, steer and stop work. 'approve': show and answer approvals; never held by an engine, a plugin or a session token. 'manage': change the install; never granted by pairing.

workspace_request.description: The folder a caller asks to work in. mode defaults to the configured one. It is validated by the workspace lane before anything is launched; what was granted is in the record's 'workspace'.

row.description: One method. params and result name this file's own definitions for the method. codes lists EVERY code the method can answer. idempotency: 'command_id' (the request carries one), 'client_key' (run.start's own key, which is its command id), 'none'. precondition: which field a request must carry to prove it read the current state. requires: the driver flags the method needs; with one missing it is refused 'unsupported' before any side effect. mcp: whether the Control MCP server offers the method as a tool, under which name, with which annotations. beta: shown as beta until its first proof is recorded. lane: who implements it.

refusal.description: An answer that is a refusal. detail says more: for 'conflict' it is one of command_id_reused (the id was used with another payload), stale_revision, stale_turn, already_resolved (someone answered first) or digest_mismatch (the digest named is not the one that was drawn); for 'unsupported' it is not_implemented (the daemon has no handler for the method yet) or the driver flag that is missing; for 'request_invalid' it names the field. The id fields echo what the request named. current_revision is given with stale_revision so a client can read again.

start_error.description: Why the launch path refused a start, under 'start_failed': a typed code and a detail. The code is the launch path's own (for example route_not_configured, launch_refused, breaker_store_unavailable, reservation_refused).

run_start_answer.description: What run.start answers today. 'started': the run, whether this was a retry of the same key ('duplicate'), and, when a Stop arrived during the launch, that Stop's answer. 'start_failed': the launch path refused or failed; 'recorded' says whether that was written, and 'start_error' carries the launch path's own code. 'start_unconfirmed': the launch may be running and the registry could not confirm it; a retry repeats this answer and never upgrades it to 'started'.

route_row.description: One row of the route inventory, as route.list answers it today (daemon/control_adapter.py, route_records; daemon/plugins.py, route_records). class says what the row is about. No bar is claimed: every row is beta, and 'blocker' says in words what stands between the row and a claim.

plugin_row.description: One installed plugin, loaded or refused, as plugin.list answers it today (daemon/plugins.py, inventory). A refused plugin has a code, a detail and its findings; a loaded one also has what it was trusted as and what it provides.

budget_row.description: DRAFT, lane QUOTA supplies the fields. What is known about one connection: its cap, what was spent in the current window (with its own quality, never 0 for unknown), when the window resets, the breaker state, and whether the login is locked.

diff.description: DRAFT, lane WORKSPACE supplies the fields. The change in a session's workspace since base_ref: every file with its status and counts; untracked files are included. patch_ref names where the text of the diff can be read, or is null when it is not kept.

doctor_report.description: DRAFT, lane INSTALL supplies the checks. What doctor found, as a list of checks. id names the check (for example interpreter.free_threaded, systemd.version, engine.binary), subject names what it was run on when there are several (an engine, a store), state is 'ok', 'warn', 'fail' or 'unknown', and 'unknown' is never reported as ok. fix is the exact step that would mend it, or null. A check reads no credential.

request.description: One request: a method of the table and its params.

exchange.description: One request with the answer it got. For a method of the table the params and the answer are that method's. A method that is not in the table is answered method_unknown.

refused_exchange.description: A request the table calls malformed (a required param is missing, or a value is out of range), with the answer the daemon gave. The params are not checked here; the answer is the method's.
